EICMA 2026 • Honda CRF1150L Africa Twin Enduro Sports Is a Tongue Twister, Weighs Less but Offers More
1979 Chevy SS Monte Mino Mixes El Camino, Monte Carlo SS, and Corvette, It'll Be a Hot Wheels Car
32 photos
Photo: Mattel
The worlds of cars and toys have always been intertwined, thanks to the few companies that have made it their lives' purpose to shrink and replicate real-world vehicles for fun and games in the hands of kids and adults alike. Usually, these toy makers treat us, on a constant basis, to replicas of existing production models, but, in some cases, they do go the extra mile and launch toys based on much rarer custom cars.
And by that I mostly mean Mattel, whose Hot Wheels brand has always produced cars and (at times) motorcycles like no others in the world. Most of them are, of course, based on production vehicles or even made up, but ever since 2018 the company has been treating us to exquisite four-wheelers based on some of the most insane custom builds in the world.
It was six years ago when the company launched the Legends Tour presented by Mobil 1, as a means to celebrate its 50th anniversary. The event kicked off as a U.S.-based competition backed by Walmart that sought to find extreme custom builds worthy of being turned into die-cast toys.
The idea caught on very rapidly and, more importantly than that, grew into something Hot Wheels now describes as the world’s largest traveling car show and global custom car competition. And you only need to look at this year's edition to quickly understand what that means.
Photo: Mattel For the 2026 Hot Wheels Legends Tour, the company's reps and their backers traveled to no less than 19 countries (in Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Latin America, and Asia Pacific) in their search for the most exquisite build, stopping no less than 12 times in North America alone.
At dedicated events, Hot Wheels designers and local automotive experts had their say on each entry in the competition, evaluating them based on a number of criteria, including authenticity, creativity, and garage spirit.
The company does not specifically say how many entries had to be judged, but we do know which came on top at the end of it all: a 1979 Chevrolet El Camino put together by Tampa-based custom-car builder Matt McEntegart.
Ok, calling this thing an El Camino is a gross understatement, as the build process required the mounting of the coupe utility vehicle's body on a modified 2008 Corvette chassis stretched by 12 inches (30 cm), and fitting it with Monte Carlo SS widebody components. When all was said and done, a modified Chevrolet V8 engine of undisclosed capabilities was stuck under the hood.
Photo: Mattel For that reason, the car as you see it in the attached gallery is nicknamed SS Monte Mino, and it required thousands of hours of work to come together, all of them completed by McEntegart himself.
The result is a mutant vehicle dressed in maroon paint with red-tinted forged carbon fiber panels designed to replicate the look and feel of a Hot Wheels diecast. It rides on massive 22-inch wheels tied to a custom suspension system which allows it to sit uncomfortably close to the ground.
The interior is custom too, as you can't have one without the other, with the design of the cabin meant to evoke 1980s styling and mix it with modern-day Corvette technology.
After declaring the SS Monte Mino the winner of the 2026 Hot Wheels Legends Tour over the past weekend, the toy maker announced it will shrink it down and turn it into a 1:64-scale die-cast collectible that will be available all over the world. On top of that, the custom car will also get its place in the Hot Wheels Garage of Legends.
Photo: Mattel It's not yet clear when the newcomer will become available, but it probably won't be that long, if we are to judge by how things unfolded in the past. As a side note, this is the first time an entry from the United States was declared a winner since the 2022 edition.
Not far behind McEntegart and his design, this year's Hot Wheels competition registered runner-ups Sandranto Hertanu (Achun Owen) from Indonesia, with a 1961 Morris Mini turned into a pickup truck, Italian Andrea Cionco with a widebody 1990 Mazda MX-5, and Chilean Andres Romero Maureira, who entered the 1992 Chevrolet Salaya SP purpose-built race car animated by a V8 good for 450 hp.
I just had to mention these other three designs, as I'll try to dig up as much information as possible about them and bring them before you in all their juicy form in upcoming stories.
Back to the SS Monte Mino, the ride joins a very select list of cars that have won the previous Hot Wheels competitions: 2JetZ (2018), The Nash (2019), 1970 Pontiac Firebird (2020), 1969 Volvo P1800 Gasser (2021), Texas Toot (2022), 1990 Mazda MX-5 Chimera (2023), 1968 Ford Falcon La Liebre (2024), and Fiat 126P Bis (2025).
